text:
FIU football highlights three consecutive seasons of bowl eligibility from 2017 to 2019
M. S. Goins
FIU football announced on Aug. 5 that it is celebrating its 25th season in 2026 by highlighting significant moments in the program's history, including three consecutive seasons of bowl eligibility from 2017 to 2019 under head coach Butch Davis.
Davis took over the program in 2017 and led the Panthers to immediate success, achieving three straight bowl appearances and a total of 23 victories during that period. In his first season, FIU finished with an overall record of 8-5 and a Conference USA record of 5-3, earning a spot in the Gasparilla Bowl—its first bowl game since the 2011 season. The team also recorded a notable turnaround at home with a 6-1 record compared to the previous season’s mark of four wins and eight losses.
Building on this foundation, FIU achieved nine wins in the following year, finishing with a conference record of six wins and two losses. The Panthers secured victories over rivals such as Middle Tennessee and Western Kentucky before capping off their season with a win against Toledo at the Bahamas Bowl on Dec. 21, highlighted by running back Anthony Jones scoring three touchdowns.
In Davis’ third year, FIU continued its consistency by winning six games overall and maintaining another strong home performance at six wins out of seven games. A key moment came when FIU defeated Miami at Marlins Park on Nov. 22, securing bowl eligibility for a third straight year before participating in the Camellia Bowl.
The upcoming season marks not only FIU’s quarter-century milestone but also reflects on past achievements including six total bowl qualifications since its inaugural campaign in 2002, along with producing NFL players like T.Y. Hilton and Jonnu Smith. As part of this celebration, fans are encouraged to follow commemorative content released across FIU Football’s social media channels.
